subject.title: [Bug P2] scheduleReconnect() has no max retry limit — infinite reconnect loop

question: Should GatewayClient keep unlimited reconnects by default and expose an opt-in maxReconnectAttempts mode, or should OpenClaw impose a default retry ceiling?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but changing reconnect defaults is compatibility-sensitive because node-host recovery may intentionally depend on indefinite reconnects.

options.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
options.body: Keep existing default behavior for long-lived node clients and add a caller-controlled maxReconnectAttempts path for short-lived clients.

options.title: Default retry ceiling
options.body: Apply a default cap for all GatewayClient users, accepting the upgrade risk for clients that currently rely on indefinite recovery.

options.title: Split listener leak only
options.body: Leave reconnect policy unchanged and only pursue cleanup if maintainers decide the reported listener/zombie accumulation is the actual bug.

recommendation.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
recommendation.body: Keep existing default behavior for long-lived node clients and add a caller-controlled maxReconnectAttempts path for short-lived clients.
